rulings.challenge_claim: The span's own close at Jer.31.40 never states a warrant for stopping there, leaving that shared boundary disclosed only from the far side, while the front seam is fully warranted by contrast.
rulings.grounds: The core defect verifies. No field of the unit gives a tier-1 reason for stopping at Jer.31.40: the rationale narrates the perimeter through the closing verse and stops, and boundary_evidence_refs carries no reference at or past Jer.32.1. The device actually standing at that seam is tier-1 and unnamed: הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.32.1, byte) is verse-initial and a member of the eleven-verse prose-sermon superscription object in the byte-swept frame inventory, and it carries a header-internal regnal date. Two corrections to the framing. First, the close is not wholly unstated: a setumah at oshb:Jer.31.40 is disclosed as closing the span (single-witness). In the Prophets that layer is tier-3 weak corroboration and is barred from driving a boundary, so no tier-1 warrant stands at the back edge, but the absolute wording overstates what is missing. Second, the contrast runs the wrong way: the front edge is the weaker of the two. Its device הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.31.38, byte) is a recurring incipit shape standing in 15 verses book-wide at skeleton tier and 5 verses at byte tier (sweep: 15 verses skeleton, 5 verses byte, MT keys), three of them inside this same chapter (oshb:Jer.31.27, oshb:Jer.31.31, oshb:Jer.31.38), and the unit carries it with no digit and with no continuity reading weighed. The span itself is not in dispute: identity numbering throughout, no contact with the book's renumbering zone or its non-Hebrew verse, and all of the unit's pointed splices re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Jer.31.38, oshb:Jer.31.39 and oshb:Jer.31.40.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: add one closing sentence naming the tier-1 device that ends the span, the prose-sermon superscription heading Jer.32.1, a member of the eleven-verse superscription-shape object, with its header-internal regnal date; and state that the setumah already disclosed in device_notes is tier-3 corroboration only, not the bound. boundary_evidence_refs: add the out-of-span verse argued by that new sentence (Jer.32.1) so every verse argued in prose outside the span is carried in the field. boundary_rationale: attach a digit-bearing sweep to the opening-incipit claim, naming the swept object, the unit and the tier (skeleton 15 verses, byte 5 verses, MT keys), and name the two chapter-internal recurrences at Jer.31.27 and Jer.31.31. No boundary change is proposed; the span stands. Tests the cure must pass: the back edge must carry a stated tier-1 warrant that survives with the parashah layer deleted entirely, and every verse argued in prose outside the span must appear in boundary_evidence_refs.

rulings.challenge_claim: A digit-bearing naming claim about the scribe is contradicted by the bytes; the opening splice is described as a voice its own first words do not carry and is glossed by two words of a seven-word run; and the confidence sits above what the seam's signals support.
rulings.grounds: All three limbs verify on bytes. Naming digit: a token-bound verse sweep of the attested pointed spelling בָּר֣וּךְ (oshb:Jer.32.12, byte) returns exactly two verses inside Jer.32.6-Jer.32.15, oshb:Jer.32.12 and בָּר֔וּךְ (oshb:Jer.32.13, byte). MT 32:14 carries no such token, and the chapter's third site stands at oshb:Jer.32.16, outside the span. The consonantal skeleton of the same name returns 23 verses book-wide (sweep: 23 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys), two of which are the passive participle at oshb:Jer.17.7 and oshb:Jer.20.14, so a count reached by implication and shipped without naming its spelling blends a name form with a lexeme. Gloss extent: the splice is the whole verse, וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ הָיָ֥ה דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.32.6, byte), seven tokens; the paired rendering covers the first two, וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ (oshb:Jer.32.6, byte), which are third-person narration. The first-person element the sentence argues from, אֵלַ֥י (oshb:Jer.32.6, byte), stands in the unglossed tail הָיָ֥ה דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.32.6, byte), so the unit's own stated warrant never surfaces in the English half of the pair. Calibration: the onset is a member of none of the three word-event objects, since the twenty-one-verse vayehi list, the eleven-verse superscription list and the four-verse topical-header list all exclude it, and the chapter carries exactly two word-event verses (Jer.32.1 and Jer.32.26). The seam rests on a person shift out of narration plus a davar clause standing outside every inventoried frame object, with tier-3 petuchah at oshb:Jer.32.5 and oshb:Jer.32.15 as its only corroboration (single-witness). Across the eight units of this cluster the confidence set is 7 medium and 1 high, and that single high rating sits on the thinnest inventoried warrant of the set. New finding, raised by neither item: a paseq falls at oshb:Jer.32.8, inside the span and in the very verse the unit splices and discusses, and no field of the unit discloses it (seg layer, count-only, single-witness), so the span-relevant mark and seg set is incomplete.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace the three-times naming sentence with the byte-true count, the scribe's name standing in exactly two verses of this span, Jer.32.12 and Jer.32.13; name the attested pointed spelling and the swept unit, drop the by-implication third site, and note that the chapter's remaining site stands at Jer.32.16 outside the span. boundary_rationale: re-cut the quote-gloss pair at Jer.32.6 so the rendering covers the whole spliced run including the first-person word-event clause, or shorten the splice to the run the rendering actually covers; the first-person element is the stated warrant and must stand on both sides of the pair. device_notes: disclose the span-relevant paseq at Jer.32.8 (seg layer, count-only, single-witness), completing the mark and seg set for the span. confidence: lower to medium unless a further tier-1 class is stated for the onset, and disclose in device_notes that the opening formula stands outside all three inventoried word-event objects. Tests the cure must pass: the corrected digit must survive a token-bound verse sweep of the named pointed spelling restricted to the span; the rendering must cover the full spliced run on read-back; the span's mark, seg and note set must be complete against the inventory; and the confidence must name the tier-1 class carrying it.

rulings.challenge_claim: One item holds that the internal cut at Jer.32.36 splits a single unchanged-speaker reply opening at Jer.32.26 and that the Hebrew of Jer.32.35 is quoted in the boundary field with no ketiv/qere note beside it; the other holds that the closing sentence attributes the high places to Molech against the construct chain it splices and against its own rendering, and that the same field slices a ketiv/qere verse with no note disclosed in it.
rulings.grounds: The two note-placement items are ONE defect reached from two directions; the boundary attack and the misattribution are DISTINCT. Misattribution UPHELD: the spliced chain reads בָּמ֨וֹת הַבַּ֜עַל (oshb:Jer.32.35, byte), the high places of the Baal, and the splice stops at the verse's ninth token; לַמֹּלֶךְ֒ (oshb:Jer.32.35, byte) is the fourteenth token of twenty-nine and stands outside the splice. The prose calls them the high places built for Molech, so sentence, splice and rendering disagree on read-back. New finding on the mechanism: the paired rendering runs on through that fourteenth token, so gloss extent EXCEEDS splice extent here, and the English half carries the name the Hebrew half does not, which is where the misattribution enters. Note placement UPHELD as one defect: the ketiv/qere pair at oshb:Jer.32.35 is disclosed only in device_notes while the slice is taken in boundary_rationale. The slice is verse-initial and the pair is verse-final at tokens 26 and 27 of 29, so no counting hazard materialised, but in the book's largest note inventory the disclosure belongs where the slicing happens. The span-relevant paseq at oshb:Jer.32.35 is disclosed in no field although the unit owns that verse (seg layer, count-only, single-witness). Boundary attack REFUTED on bytes: an explicit addressee shift stands at the seam. The second-person plural pronoun אַתֶּ֣ם (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte) makes its first appearance in the reply there; a pointed scan of MT 32:26-32:35 returns 0 second-person plural pronouns, verb endings or suffixes across those ten verses, and the one skeleton lookalike inside them is the third-person object pronoun אֹתָם֙ (oshb:Jer.32.33, byte), a homograph at skeleton tier only. A third-to-second person turn is an explicit addressee shift, a ruled tier-1 internal-cut class, so the cut does not rest on a turn particle alone. The declines one seam later are consistent rather than inconsistent: the same pronoun recurs at oshb:Jer.32.43 (byte), so the second-person addressee is already live across Jer.32.42-32.43 and no shift occurs there (sweep: 2 verses carrying that pronoun across Jer.32.26-Jer.32.44, byte tier, MT keys, at oshb:Jer.32.36 and oshb:Jer.32.43). A setumah at oshb:Jer.32.35 falls at the same seam as tier-3 corroboration (single-witness). The onset is inventory-confirmed: וַיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ (oshb:Jer.32.26, byte) is verse-initial and a member of the twenty-one-verse vayehi word-event object.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: correct the closing content sentence so it names the deity its own spliced construct chain names, and bring the pair to equal extent, either extending the splice through the clause the rendering covers or cutting the rendering back to the splice's own end, so that sentence, splice and rendering agree on read-back. boundary_rationale: state the ketiv/qere note for Jer.32.35 in the same field where the verse is sliced, with its single-witness label and the observation that the slice is verse-initial while the pair is verse-final, so a reader can check the slice falls clear of the note. device_notes: add the span-relevant paseq at Jer.32.35 (seg layer, count-only, single-witness) so the span's disclosure set is complete. strongest_rejected_alternative: strengthen the stated ground to name the third-to-second person addressee turn at Jer.32.36 rather than resting on the turn particle and a reintroduced construction. No boundary change is proposed and none is required: the cut at Jer.32.36 stands. Tests the cure must pass: reading the corrected sentence back against its own splice and its own rendering must agree on every named object; the span's mark, seg and note set must be complete against the inventory; and the span must be unchanged.

rulings.challenge_claim: An exclusivity sentence enumerates three recurrence sites under a single byte label when only two of them are byte-identical, and the closing warrant sentence attributes the bound to the chapter division.
rulings.grounds: Tier mixing verified exactly. The run אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte) is byte-identical at oshb:Jer.32.43 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier, MT keys) and returns those same 2 verses at accent-stripped tier. At the third site the run reads אֲשֶׁר֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹֽמְרִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.33.10, byte), differing in accentuation and carrying an added meteg; it therefore fails byte and also fails accent-stripped, since that tier strips cantillation but retains meteg, and it matches only at the consonantal skeleton (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys, at oshb:Jer.32.36, oshb:Jer.32.43 and oshb:Jer.33.10). The sentence carries one byte label across all three sites while asserting that the construction stands nowhere else in the book, so a tier label is doing the work of the exclusivity sweep at the one site where that label is false. The construction-level exclusivity is itself sound at 3 verses; only the tier is wrong. Chapter-division attribution verified. Chapter and verse divisions are tier-4 and are never evidence in either direction, so a bound may not be attributed to one. The substantive device is named in the same sentence, the second word-event at Jer.33.1, whose MT verse is verse-initial and a member of the twenty-one-verse vayehi object, so the warrant exists and only its attribution is misplaced, which is why this stays low rather than rising. Recorded in the unit's favour on re-derivation: the closing captivity-reversal run אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שְׁבוּתָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.32.44, byte) is byte-identical in exactly two verses (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier, MT keys, at oshb:Jer.32.44 and oshb:Jer.33.26), matching the unit's own digit, and the span's mark and seg disclosures are complete against the inventory.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: split the recurrence sentence by tier, byte-identical at Jer.32.36 and Jer.32.43 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier) and consonantal-skeleton-only at Jer.33.10 (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier), noting that the third site fails accent-stripped because that tier retains meteg, and attach the nowhere-else claim to the skeleton tier where its three-verse digit holds. boundary_rationale: restate the closing sentence so the bound is attributed to the word-event formula at Jer.33.1 alone, and delete the chapter division as the stated bound. Tests the cure must pass: every tier label in the recurrence sentence must reproduce its stated site list on a re-run sweep at that tier, with the exclusivity digit and the tier standing in the same sentence; and the closing sentence must name only a tier-1 device as the bound, surviving with all chapter-division wording deleted.
